Thanks,
Daniel

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700

Hi Daniel — thanks for the heads up and the sample log.

Short answer: we observed a routing backlog caused by a misapplied autoscaling policy during a transient GPU contention event in the us-west-2 pool that serves your dedicated instances. That caused request queuing and then a subset of timeouts. We are still validating exact root cause correlations with kernel-level metrics.

Planned immediate deliverables for you by EOD:
- A 1-page customer-friendly timeline of the event (what happened, duration, impact).
- Action items we will take this week to prevent recurrence and an estimated completion window.
- A set of short-term mitigations you can enable (temporary routing to warm capacity, increased retry-window).

I'll loop in Grace and Hannah for the technical timeline and a brief remediation checklist. Expect a technical appendix and the CSV timeline attached once we collate data.

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Team — quick internal note on findings so far (summary for Sean to share with Starlark):

Timeline (preliminary):
- 08:28 PDT: Autoscaler applied an unexpected policy change during a maintenance job; two worker pools briefly reported 100% GPU utilization.
- 08:30-08:52 PDT: Requests queued leading to increased tail latency; some requests hit the client-side timeout (60s) and retried.
- 08:52 PDT: Fallback routing engaged automatically for most traffic; global capacity reclaimed by 09:00 PDT.

Probable root cause: a race in autoscaling policy refresh + a maintenance task that triggered suboptimal kernel placement on a subset of nodes. The kernel-level contention amplified under the typical morning traffic spike.

Immediate corrective actions (this afternoon):
- Revert the autoscaler policy change that rolled at 08:20 (Grace) — ETA 2h.
- Run targeted regression test on kernel placement under synthetic load (Hannah) — ETA 24h.
- Add a temporary guard that prevents policy refresh during maintenance windows (Marissa owning ops config) — ETA 48h.

Attachments to prepare: starlark_timeline.csv (per-request timestamps), investigation-notes.pdf (engineer writeup), service-metrics.png (graphs).

I'll prepare a one-page timeline and a short customer-friendly summary for Sean to send.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Reliability Engineering

Adding detail from the kernel and serving runtime analysis (for technical appendix):

- During the maintenance window a subsidiary kernel selection path mistakenly favored a high-latency kernel on 6/24 nodes; under load, KV cache misses amplified the latency.
- Error rates spiked in a correlated manner with the per-GPU queue length metric; we have per-request traces in the attached CSV.
- No customer data exposure; all requests were processed within our secure environment.

Recommended post-incident tasks (owners + preliminary ETAs):
1) Hard block autoscaler policy refresh during maintenance windows (Marissa) — 48h.
2) Kernel placement validation test integrated into canary (Hannah) — 72h.
3) Improve alerting on per-GPU queue length with a 5-min rolling average spike alarm (Grace) — 24h.
4) Share final customer-facing timeline and a short appendix for compliance (Sean) — EOD tomorrow.

Hi Daniel — thanks for your patience while we investigated. Below is a concise customer-facing summary, a timeline, and the actions we'll take. The attachments linked include the per-request CSV and the internal investigation notes for your engineering and compliance teams.

Executive summary:
- What happened: A maintenance-triggered autoscaler policy refresh coincided with a transient GPU contention event in the us-west-2 serving pool, causing request queuing and elevated tail latency. A subset of requests timed out and triggered client retries.
- Impact: 22-minute degradation window (2027-05-17 08:30–08:52 PDT). Approximately 0.8% of production requests for your inference route experienced timeouts; no data exfiltration or unauthorized access was detected.
- Current status: Configuration reverted and traffic routing restored; monitoring continues with tighter thresholds.

Timeline (UTC / PDT):
- 2027-05-17 15:28 UTC (08:28 PDT): Autoscaler policy refresh initiated during maintenance job.
- 2027-05-17 15:30–15:52 UTC (08:30–08:52 PDT): Elevated per-request latency and queueing observed; some requests timed out on client side.
- 2027-05-17 15:52 UTC (08:52 PDT): Automated fallback routing reduced load on affected nodes; capacity reclaimed by 09:00 PDT.

Actions we will take (owners & ETA):
- Immediate (completed): Reverted policy change that triggered the refresh (Grace) — completed 2027-05-17 11:10 PDT.
- 24–72 hours: Add a guard to prevent policy refresh during maintenance windows and add a 5-minute rolling GPU-queue alert (Marissa/Grace) — ETA 2027-05-19.
- 72 hours: Integrate kernel placement validation into the canary tests (Hannah) — ETA 2027-05-22.
- 2 weeks: Run a synthetic load test against the warm pool to validate behavior under the morning traffic profile (Grace/Hannah) — ETA 2027-05-31.

Short-term customer mitigations you can enable (optional):
- Temporarily route a portion of traffic to warm reserved capacity during your morning spike (coordinate with Marissa).
- Slightly increase client-side retry window to absorb tail spikes while we deploy permanent guards.

Attachments (attached to this message):
- starlark_timeline.csv — per-request timestamps and latencies (CSV)
- investigation-notes.pdf — technical appendix (PDF)
- service-metrics.png — latency and queue-length graphs (PNG)

Next steps from Redwood:
- We'll confirm completion of the 24–72h items and share a short verification report once the canary validation passes.
- If you would like a joint post-incident call to walk through the appendix and validate test plans with your SREs, we can schedule one; suggest Thu 2027-05-20 10:00 PDT.

If you need anything sooner, reply here or ping me directly.

Best regards,
